properties.natural_language: All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-LC-DATA-SOURCE to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: All light client headers must pass: (1) blob gas field validation for pre-Deneb epochs (must be zero), (2) execution payload emptiness check for pre-Capella epochs, (3) Merkle branch verification of execution root against beacon body root. Headers from any source are fully untrusted.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Block header excess_blob_gas must exactly match calc_excess_blob_gas computation with timestamp-based fork boundary reset. Mismatch must result in block rejection. Special attention needed at fork boundary where excess_blob_gas resets to 0.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-PRECOMPILE-CALLER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Input must be exactly 213 bytes. Final flag byte must be exactly 0 or 1. Gas cost = rounds * 1 must be available. High rounds values (up to 2^32-1) are valid but gas-metered. All input fields (h, m, t, f) are attacker-controlled and must produce deterministic RFC 7693 output.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-EL-VIA-ENGINE-API to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: The block_access_list_root provided by EL must be validated by CL. At fork transition it is initialized to Root() (zero). Post-fork, CL must verify EL-provided values are consistent with execution payload content.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-CL-VIA-ENGINE-API to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: JWT authentication required. ForkchoiceState must be validated: headBlockHash must reference a known valid payload, safeBlockHash must be ancestor of head, finalizedBlockHash must be consistent. Payload attributes must have valid timestamp. Message ordering must be enforced sequentially.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-ENGINE-API-CALLER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: All requests must present a valid JWT bearer token signed with the shared secret. Invalid or missing JWT must result in immediate rejection. The shared secret must be securely generated and stored. Communication should occur over localhost or trusted network.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-DAPP-VIA-WALLET to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: DApp-provided ABIs are untrusted. Wallets must: (1) validate interface spec version, (2) perform case-sensitive address matching, (3) optionally verify against trusted ABI database, (4) clearly indicate to users when ABI source is unverified. Decoded calldata display must not be presented as authoritative.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-MALICIOUS-DAPP to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Wallets must assume all DApp-provided ABIs could be misleading. Users must be warned that decoded transaction details are only as trustworthy as the providing DApp. Wallets should indicate verified vs. unverified ABI sources visually.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-WALLET-USER to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: User approval drives transaction signing. Wallet must present accurate information about trust level of decoded data. Users may be misled by malicious ABIs; wallet UI must distinguish verified from unverified decoded calldata.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-TRUSTED-ABI-DB to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Database responses are delivered over HTTPS. Database may not have entries for all contracts. Absence of verification does not imply malicious intent. Wallet must handle missing entries gracefully and indicate unverified status to user.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-GOSSIP-PEER to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Full validation pipeline required: (1) correct subnet routing (column_index % SUBNET_COUNT == subnet_id), (2) temporal bounds (not future, within finalized range), (3) proposer signature verification, (4) KZG commitments inclusion Merkle proof, (5) batch KZG proof verification, (6) proposer index matches expected shuffling. REJECT for cryptographic failures, IGNORE for timing issues.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-REQUESTING-PEER to Consensus Layer (CL) must be validated according to: Request parameters must be validated: start_slot and count within data_column_serve_range, request size within MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB limits, block_root since minimum_request_epoch. Oversized requests must be rejected. Resource unavailability (code 3) returned for data outside serve range.

All data crossing the trust boundary from EXT-HEX-INPUT-SOURCE to Execution Layer (EL) must be validated according to: Input must contain only valid hex characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) after optional 0x prefix.
